node.title: Re^2: wrap abbreviations in XML element
node.author: LexPl
node.doctext:
many thanks for your detailed feedback which I will consume bit by bit :)

In a short test with slight adaptations to your script:

  1. my $doc = XML::LibXML->load_xml(string => <<'XML'); hello, foobar world! a.!!!emsp14;A. foooa.!!!hairsp;A. XML
  2. my $re = qr/a\.(!!!emsp14;|!!!hairsp;)A\./;
  3. my $e = $doc->createElement('abbrev');

I got the following output:
hello, foobar world! a.!!!emsp14;A.!!!emsp14; foooa.!!!hairsp;A.!!!hairsp;

As you will see, the separating whitespace is repeated after the "abbrev" element. Why do I use "!!!emsp14;" for the entity  ? I want to prevent that such entities will be resolved by an XML parser and I want to manipulate my data independently from a DTD.
